svg.title: iOS · Stills import · the question · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/StillsImportSheet.swift over AppModel.stillsImportQuestion — the question Create ▸ Import photos… asks once the pick has resolved to two or more files and before any copy: a shoot, or a photo each. The reading is ImportedStills.reading (Kit, ImportedStills+Reading.swift; docs/import-classification.md §3): a SHOOT is a clean set — one name sequence, every frame on one beat, the only irregularity a pause whose beat continues — and PHOTOS is suggested only when no beat of 24 frames exists anywhere. Title = the count; the line under it = the files' own reading (the one folder they came from · formats · body · first shutter to last). Two rows say what each answer MAKES, in numbers, so Photos on a 5030-file folder reads as the 5030 projects it would be. Import is the default action (⏎) and Cancel (⎋) is always reachable; the sheet is not dismissable by swipe or click-away — the import is suspended on a continuation inside runStillsImport, and an answer is what starts the copy. LL_IMPORT_STILLS=<folder> with no LL_IMPORT_ANSWER stages it; LL_IMPORT_ANSWER=shoot|photos|cancel answers it headless. THIS FILE: the clean state. The set reads as a shoot, so the Interval shoot row is pre-selected and tagged Detected — Auto is the pre-selection, not a third row, because a pre-selected row shows the answer where an 'Auto' label would make the person guess what it will do. One tap imports. Drawn on Charles_ARW once its stray Lightroom render is out: 306 ARW, Sony ILCE-7M4, 3.62 s ± 0.02, 18 min, one evening. Verified 2026-09-15 against the running app on a 30-frame slice of the same folder (the layout; the 306-frame reading is the Kit's test). On the phone the sheet is full height like the archive sheet — its 380-wide content sits centred in the 393-pt screen with the two buttons anchored at the bottom above the home indicator, and the space between the rows and the buttons is the sheet's, not a control. iPad shares this file (a form sheet). Verified 2026-09-15 on an iPhone 16 Pro simulator (LetsLapse Fresh device, LL_IMPORT_STILLS).

g.text: One project of 306 frames, 3.6 s apart
